newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Fischler says EU stands firm in U.S. meat talks.
newsitem.headline: Fischler says EU stands firm in U.S. meat talks.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday that the EU could not compromise consumer health by making concessions to the United States over meat inspection rules.

The main outstanding issue in negotiations, due to resume in Washington on Tuesday, is over poultry decontamination. The EU says the U.S. method of decontaminating chicken carcasses by dipping them in chlorinated water is unacceptable.
"We don't want to say to consumers that we are making trade concessions when scientists say there are health risks," Fischler told a news conference after a two-day EU farm ministers meeting.
On April 1, the EU implemented new inspection rules blocking U.S. poultry imports worth some $50 million annually.
U.S. retaliation was delayed two weeks until April 30 because of progress in the talks but on Monday U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman warned that there would be no more extensions.
If no "veterinary equivalency" agreement is reached by the end-month deadline, the U.S. has said it will block imports of U.S. meat, mainly Danish pigmeat, worth some $300 million annually.
